caption: 1 · The twelve base themes (the person, 2026-11-22), Sage the default; each is paper, ink and one accent; marks and folder colors stay yours
2 · The twelve in dark: each keeps its accent, lifted for a dark page
3 · Page surface: Paper, Sepia, Night or your own colors, for the reader and pages only; the theme stays
4 · Scripture faces side by side at reading size (all free and open licensed); Crimson Pro is the fifth, drawn on request
5 · Reading: no rail, no chrome but a quiet top line; the dock waits at the bottom edge
6 · The dock up: home, the apps, Settings; open apps carry a dot; the name shows on hover
7 · A click on Notebook opens it on this desk beside what is there (or brings it forward); the dock sinks as the pointer leaves
8 · Right-click an app in the dock: its recent items, New window, Keep in dock or Remove
9 · Static taskbar (Settings › Dock › Always shown): the same apps, always visible, the reader stops above it
10 · Settings › Dock: on hover or always shown, the edge (bottom by default; here left, as it would look), growing on hover, the apps' order
11 · The Workbench home: where you left off, today's reading, open questions, recent pages; one click resumes each
12 · Continue reading: the Bible at the verse you left, lit briefly; back returns to the Workbench
13 · Together A, Snap: drag an app's title to the top edge for layouts (halves, two-thirds, thirds, quarters); like Windows snap layouts
14 · Together B, Stage: the working set in the middle; other sets wait at the left as small cards, one click swaps them in (like Stage Manager)
15 · Together C, Desks: a named, saved arrangement of apps per task; switching desks swaps the whole screen; nothing stays open unseen
16 · Keys: holding Ctrl shows each app's number on the dock
17 · Dragging a title: it lifts and eases to a handy size under the pointer; the others hold
18 · Over John 1's right side: the others make room live; the outline names the new column
19 · Over John 1's top: its column splits live; the outline says Above John 1
20 · Over John 1's middle: the outline says Swap with John 1
21 · At the desk's left edge: a new column there
22 · Let go: it lands exactly where the outline was, on the spring
23 · Dragging the gap between two: both resize live and stop at the smallest size
24 · At the window's top edge: four layouts drop down in glass; the one under the pointer lights
25 · Let go on Thirds: the desk arranges itself in three
26 · Onto another desk's name: it rings; let go and the bubble moves there
27 · A drop that would overfill: the oldest bubble dims and the outline says it goes to the tray
28 · Ctrl+Shift+→ trades the focused bubble with its neighbour (Ctrl+arrows only move the focus)
29 · Opening more than fits: the bubble used longest ago flies into a pill at the dock's end
30 · Clicking a pill: it grows back out of the pill beside the focused bubble
31 · Bubble ⋯ › Put in the tray
32 · Three passages, each its own bubble with its own ← →
33 · Bubble ⋯ › Gather: the other Bible bubbles fold in as columns
34 · ⇱ pop out: a gathered column becomes its own bubble again
35 · Clicking a word: its entry grows out of the word into a place beside; ↖ John 1 in its title
36 · Clicking ↖ John 1: the bubble it came from rings and takes focus
37 · Alt+click: the same bubble becomes the entry; ← returns to the passage
38 · Options › Ask: a glass menu at the pointer: Beside, Here, On a new desk
39 · Opening something already open: that bubble rings instead of a copy (R11)
40 · ◷ History: a glass bar with the scope, the view and the steps from earlier to now
41 · Scrubbing back: the desk replays on the springs, tinted warm as the past
42 · Let go and act: a branch begins; the later steps are kept
43 · The map: dots, a second lane where the branch began; click a dot to go there
44 · Bubble ⋯ › This bubble's history
45 · Scrubbing back past an edit: the page shows its words as they were
46 · Ctrl+Z on the desk: one step back, replayed on the springs
47 · The pointer at the bottom edge: the glass dock rises
48 · Along the dock: the icons swell like a lens under the pointer; the name floats above
49 · Clicking Notebook in the dock: the icon bounces and the bubble grows out of it
50 · Clicking a desk: the green pill slides to it; its bubbles slide in from that side
51 · + makes a new empty desk; double-click a name to rename it
52 · Workbench in the dock: where you left off, today's reading, an open question, every desk
53 · Phone: each bubble a full card to swipe; the dock always shown
55 · Double-click a title (or ⤢, or Ctrl+Enter): it grows over the desk on the spring; the desk waits underneath, dimmed
56 · Settled in full view: ⤡, Esc or another double-click springs it back to exactly where it was
57 · Back on the desk: the same place, the same size, nothing else moved
54 · Glass: a soft highlight follows the pointer; what lies behind bends through it
